pages.title: How to Export Order Details from WooCommerce to Excel
pages.content:
Need to review or report on your store’s orders in a spreadsheet? In this guide I will show you how to export WooCommerce order details to Excel, including information such as order dates, customer names, products, totals, and order statuses.

You can use the exported data to sort and analyze orders outside WordPress or share it with your team. Follow the steps below to export the order details you need.

## Step 1. Install WP Sheet Editor for WooCommerce Orders

This plugin allows you to manage your WooCommerce order details in a spreadsheet. You can use advanced search, bulk edit, export and import orders.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download WooCommerce Orders Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=5416&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=export-order-details-woocommerce-excel#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/woocommerce-orders-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=export-order-details-woocommerce-excel)

## Step 2. Open the Orders spreadsheet

Start by opening the WooCommerce orders spreadsheet. Go to **WP Sheet Editor > Edit orders,** and you’ll see all your WooCommerce orders’ data displayed in the spreadsheet.

![export-order-details-woocommerce-excel](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14101351/export-woocommerce-order-details-to-excel-1.png)

## Step 3. Open the Export tool

Open the **Export** tool.

![export-order-details-woocommerce-excel](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14101425/export-woocommerce-order-details-to-excel-2.png)

## Step 4. Export order details to Excel (XLSX)

Set up the export settings to download your WooCommerce orders in an Excel file (XLSX):

- What columns do you want to export: You can export specific columns, all columns, or all the columns that are currently active in the spreadsheet.
- **Which rows do you want to export:** We will export all the rows. You can export all orders, only manually selected orders, or all orders from a specific search (by status, billing data, specific products, by coupon used, etc.)
- **What app will you use to edit this file:** Microsoft Excel (XLSX)
- **Name of this export:** You can add a name to this export and run it later again with one click.
- **Optional:** You can export all order details in one row, or tick the **Export every product (line item) as separate rows** checkbox.
- Click on **Start new export.**

![export-order-details-woocommerce-excel](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14101518/export-woocommerce-order-details-to-excel-3.png)

Once the Excel file containing your order details has been downloaded into your computer, you can open it with Excel. Below you can see we have exported our orders.

![export-order-details-woocommerce-excel](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14101555/export-woocommerce-order-details-to-excel-4.png)

This is how you can export your WooCommerce order details to Microsoft Excel file using WP Sheet Editor for WooCommerce Orders.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download WooCommerce Orders Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=5416&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=export-order-details-woocommerce-excel#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/woocommerce-orders-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=export-order-details-woocommerce-excel)

pages.title: How to Find Images Used as Featured Images in WordPress
pages.content:
Finding images that are currently being used as **featured images in WordPress** isn’t easy when you have a large Media Library. WordPress lets you upload and manage media files, but it doesn’t provide a built-in search filter for finding images based on whether they are assigned as featured images.

This becomes even more difficult on websites with hundreds or thousands of images, especially when you manage different types of content such as blog posts, WooCommerce products, pages, courses, or custom post types.

In this guide, you’ll learn **how to find images used as featured images in WordPress** and how to filter those images based on the type of content they’re associated with. This can help you identify which media files are being used, find featured images for specific post types, and manage your WordPress Media Library more efficiently.

We’ll use the **WP Sheet Editor – Media Library** plugin. It displays your WordPress media files in a spreadsheet and provides advanced search and filtering tools for finding specific images and understanding how they’re being used on your website.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download Media Library Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=4933&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=find-featured-images-wordpress#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=find-featured-images-wordpress)
After installing and activating the plugin, go to **WP Sheet Editor > Edit Media** in your WordPress dashboard. This opens your Media Library in the spreadsheet editor.

![WordPress Media Library opened in WP Sheet Editor](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002028/search-featured-images-wordpress-1.jpg)

## Open the Search tool

WordPress doesn’t normally let you search the Media Library based on an image’s role in your content. For example, you can’t use the standard Media Library search to find every image that is currently assigned as a featured image.

WP Sheet Editor solves this by providing an advanced **Search** tool with filters that can identify images based on how they’re used in WordPress.

This means you can search for media files that are being used as featured images instead of manually opening posts, products, or other content to check which image is assigned to each one.

![WP Sheet Editor advanced Search tool for WordPress media files](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002202/search-featured-images-wordpress-5.jpg)

## Find all images used as featured images

If your goal is to find **every image in the Media Library that is being used as a featured image**, you can use the advanced filters in the Search tool.

1. Check **Enable advanced filters**.
2. Check **Is image used as featured image?**.
3. Click **Run search**.

![WordPress filter for finding images used as featured images](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002138/search-featured-images-wordpress-4.jpg)

WP Sheet Editor will filter the media library and show the images that are currently assigned as featured images. This can include featured images used by different types of WordPress content.

![find-featured-images-wordpress](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002114/search-featured-images-wordpress-3.jpg)

## Find featured images by post type

Sometimes you don’t want to find every featured image on the website. You may only be interested in images used by a particular type of content.

For example, you might want to find:

- Featured images assigned to WordPress blog posts
- Featured images used by WooCommerce products
- Images assigned to pages
- Featured images used by courses
- Images associated with a custom post type

You can combine the post type filter with the featured image filter to narrow down the results.

In the **Search** tool:

1. Select the relevant post type from the **Files associated to** dropdown. You can select products, posts, pages, courses, or another available post type.
2. Check **Enable advanced filters**.
3. Check **Is image used as featured image?**.
4. Click **Run search**.

![Filter WordPress featured images by post type](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002455/search-featured-images-wordpress-6.jpg)

WP Sheet Editor will display all the images associated with the selected post type.

![find-featured-images-wordpress](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/01002202/search-featured-images-wordpress-5.jpg)

## Why search for images used as featured images?

Knowing where your media files are being used can be useful when you’re managing a large WordPress website. Instead of browsing individual posts or products, you can search the Media Library and identify images based on their relationship to your content.

For example, this can help when you’re reviewing your featured images, organizing a large media library, working with WooCommerce product images, or trying to determine whether a particular image is being used on your site.

## Manage WordPress featured images from the Media Library

The standard WordPress Media Library provides basic tools for finding uploaded files, but it doesn’t offer advanced filters for every way an image is used. **WP Sheet Editor – Media Library** adds spreadsheet-style management and advanced search capabilities to make this type of media management easier.

With the featured image filter, you can search across your media files and identify images currently assigned to posts, products, pages, courses, and other post types. You can also combine the filter with a specific post type to get more targeted results.

This makes it easier to understand how images are being used across your WordPress website without manually checking each piece of content.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download Media Library Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=4933&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=find-featured-images-wordpress#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=find-featured-images-wordpress)

pages.title: How to Generate WordPress Image Alt Text with AI in Bulk
pages.category: Generate Wordpress Image Alt Text Ai Bulk
pages.content:
You can **generate WordPress image alt text with AI in bulk** instead of writing alt text manually for every image in your Media Library. With [WP Sheet Editor – Media Library](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/) and [WP Sheet Editor – AI](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/ai/), you can use a multimodal AI model to analyze your images and automatically generate descriptive alt text for hundreds or thousands of WordPress images.

This is especially useful if your WordPress Media Library contains images with missing or deficient alt text. Instead of opening each image individually and writing a description, you can filter images without alt text, send the images to an AI model, and generate unique alt text for all matching images in bulk.

In this guide, you’ll learn how to:

- Generate alt text for WordPress images using AI.
- Use an AI model to analyze images and write descriptive alt text.
- Find WordPress images with missing or empty alt text.
- Generate alt text for hundreds of images at once.
- Customize the AI prompt used to generate image alt text.
- Use different AI providers and multimodal models with WP Sheet Editor AI.

## Tools to Generate WordPress Image Alt Text with AI

The process uses two WP Sheet Editor plugins:

**WP Sheet Editor – Media Library** lets you manage WordPress Media Library files in a spreadsheet, making it easy to search, filter, and edit image metadata in bulk.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download Media Library Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=4933&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk)
**WP Sheet Editor – AI** is a service that adds AI-powered content generation to WP Sheet Editor spreadsheets. You can use it to generate or rewrite WordPress content and custom fields, including image alt text.

You can sign up here:

[Sign up to the WP Sheet Editor - AI Service](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=41738&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/ai/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk)
The AI generation is handled through your external AI provider’s API key and the**Bulk AI API**. This allows you to process many images without manually sending individual requests. WP Sheet Editor processes the requests in batches, helping you handle large numbers of images without the timeouts or PHP memory problems that can occur with a traditional many-requests-at-a-time process.

## Set Up an AI Provider and Multimodal Model

Before generating alt text, configure an AI provider and a model that can understand images.

For this example, we’ll use OpenAI with the **GPT-4o** model. You can use a different provider and model as long as it supports image input and is compatible with the supported OpenAI API format.

A multimodal model is important because the AI needs to **see and analyze the image** before it can generate useful alt tag. A text-only AI model cannot inspect the contents of an image.

**WP Sheet Editor – AI** allows you to configure multiple providers and models. This means you can use different AI models for different tasks depending on your requirements and budget.

To set up your provider and model:

1. Go to **WP Sheet Editor > AI > Settings**.
2. Select a provider that accepts Multimodal like OpenRouter, LM Studio, or your custom OpenAI-compatible provider.
3. Select your preferred model.
4. Add your external provider API Key.
5. Save the changes.

![WP Sheet Editor AI provider settings with OpenAI and multimodal model options](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29204636/ai-provider-setup.png)

**Compatible AI Providers:**

- OpenAI
- OpenRouter
- LM Studio
- Google Gemini Nano Banana
- Custom (OpenAI-Compatible)

## Open the WordPress Media Library Spreadsheet

Once your AI provider and model are configured, open your WordPress Media Library spreadsheet by going to **WP Sheet Editor > Edit Media**.

![WordPress Media Library spreadsheet showing image files and the Alt Text column](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200405/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-1.jpg)

Instead of managing each image through the standard WordPress Media Library interface, you’ll see your media files as rows in a spreadsheet. Image information, including the **Alt Text** field, can be searched, filtered, and edited from the spreadsheet.

This makes the spreadsheet especially useful when you need to **bulk edit image alt text in WordPress**.

## Option 1: Generate Alt Texts in the Spreadsheet

You can generate alt text directly from the spreadsheet by using an AI prompt. Go to the **Alt text** column to start generating alt tag.

![WP Sheet Editor spreadsheet showing how to generate image alt text with an AI prompt](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200431/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-2.jpg)

To use AI in a cell, start the value with 
```
AI:
```

 followed by your prompt. Your prompt can reference the image in the **Preview** column so the AI knows which image it needs to analyze.

```
AI: Describe the image in the $Preview$ column and generate concise, descriptive alt text.
```

The column name is enclosed between **dollar signs** so WP Sheet Editor AI knows which field to use as part of the prompt.

You can use the same approach to reference other columns or fields. This gives you control over the information provided to the AI when generating your alt text.

When you press **Enter**, the AI model receives the image and analyzes its contents before generating the requested alt text.

### Customize the AI Prompt for Better Alt Text

You don’t have to use a generic prompt. You can tell the AI exactly how you want your WordPress image alt text to be written.

For example, you can instruct the model to:

- Keep the alt text concise.
- Describe the main subject of the image.
- Include important visible details.
- Avoid unnecessary information.
- Write naturally for WordPress accessibility.
- Avoid beginning every description with phrases such as “image of” or “picture of.”

The more specific your prompt is, the more consistently the AI can follow your preferred format.

## Option 2: Bulk Generate WordPress Alt Text Using AI

If you have hundreds or thousands of images, generating alt text one image at a time isn’t practical. Instead, you can first find the images that need alt text and the generate the alt tags for all of them.

In the Media Library spreadsheet, open the **Search** tool, which will allows you to filter the **Alt Text** field to find images where the field is empty.

![generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200528/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-4.jpg)

In this example, our site hast images only, so there’s no need to add an additional file-format filter. If your Media Library contains other types of files, you can add additional filters to narrow the results to images.

In this case, just tick the **Enable advanced filters** checkbox and select these values:

- **Field:** Alt text
- **Operator:** =
- **Value:** Leave this field empty.

Once you select the search criteria, click on **Run search.**

![WP Sheet Editor Search tool filtering images with empty Alt Text fields](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200550/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-5.jpg)

After applying the filter, the spreadsheet will show the images that currently have no alt text.

![WordPress Media Library spreadsheet filtered to images without alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200615/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-6.jpg)

Now open the **Bulk Edit** tool.

![WP Sheet Editor Bulk Edit tool for generating image alt text with AI](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200642/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-7.jpg)

Once there, select these values to bulk write image alt texts with AI:

- **Select the rows that you want to** update: Edit all the rows from my current search
- **What field do you want to edit:** Alt text
- **Select type of edit:** AI Prompt
- **AI Provider:** Select the AI provider and model you want to execute this task.
- **Prompt:** Enter the prompt you want. **Note.** If you want to save a global prompt to reuse it as many times as you want without writing the prompt each time, you can follow this [guide](https://wpsheeteditor.com/ai-global-prompts/).
- Use the **Show preview** button if you want to see the result before running the bulk generation of alt tags.
- If everything looks OK, click on **Execute Now.**

![WP Sheet Editor Bulk Edit settings for generating alt text with an AI prompt](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29200704/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-8.jpg)

Once the process is complete, you will see see that all your images have proper alt texts.

![WordPress images with AI-generated alt text in the Media Library spreadsheet](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/29205842/generate-alt-texts-with-ai-9.jpg)

Writing alt texts manually can become a repetitive task when a website has a large Media Library. AI can help automate this work by analyzing each image and generating a description based on its visual content.

Bulk AI generation is particularly useful when:

- Your WordPress website has hundreds or thousands of images.
- Many existing images have missing alt text.
- You recently migrated a website and need to update image metadata.
- You want to review and improve existing image descriptions.
- You need a faster way to add descriptive alt text to a large Media Library.

Instead of opening each media attachment individually, you can find the images that need attention, apply an AI prompt, and process them together.

**Ready to generate image alt text with AI?** Use WP Sheet Editor – AI to automate alt text generation across your WordPress Media Library.

You can sign up here:

[Sign up to the WP Sheet Editor - AI Service](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=41738&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/ai/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=generate-wordpress-image-alt-text-ai-bulk)

		You can receive instant help in the live chat during business hours, or [you can contact us](https://wpsheeteditor.com/company/contact/) and we will help you via email.

pages.title: Easy LearnDash Google Sheets Integration
pages.content:
Connect [LearnDash](https://www.liquidweb.com/software/learndash/) to Google Sheets to export, import, review, and update courses, lessons, quizzes, questions, and exams in bulk.

[WP Sheet Editor](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/courses-spreadsheet/) and [Google Sheets Sync](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/google-sheets/) give you a spreadsheet interface for managing LearnDash content. You can use it to edit large amounts of data, plan course content, review your LMS, or prepare data for a migration.

## What can you manage?

- **Courses:** Titles, content, access settings, pricing, categories, tags, certificates, and other course fields.
- **Lessons:** Content, video URLs, course assignments, ordering, materials, timers, and drip schedules.
- **Topics:** Topic content and course or lesson relationships.
- **Quizzes:** Quiz settings, passing percentages, points, and course or lesson relationships.
- **Questions:** Question text, types, points, answers, hints, and quiz relationships.
- **Exams:** Supported exam data and settings.

## What can you do with Google Sheets?

### Export LearnDash data

Export LearnDash content to Google Sheets when you need to review, report on, or edit your LMS data. You can filter the data before exporting it, so you only work with the records you need.

### Import LearnDash data

Prepare your LearnDash data in Google Sheets and import it into WordPress. This can save time when creating new courses or updating many existing items at once.

### Review your course catalog

Use Google Sheets filters and sorting to find incomplete or inconsistent data. For example, you can look for missing video URLs, incorrect course assignments, or quiz settings that need to be changed.

### Collaborate on curriculum

Share LearnDash data with your curriculum team in Google Sheets. Team members can review course structures and prepare content without having to open and edit each item individually in WordPress.

## LearnDash Google Sheets tutorials

These guides cover specific LearnDash workflows:

- [Import LearnDash Courses from Google Sheets](https://wpsheeteditor.com/learndash-import-courses-google-sheets/)
- [Export LearnDash Courses to Google Sheets](https://wpsheeteditor.com/export-learndash-courses-google-sheets/)
- [Export LearnDash Lessons to Google Sheets](https://wpsheeteditor.com/export-learndash-lesssons-google-sheets/)
- [Export LearnDash Quizzes, Questions, and Exams to Google Sheets](https://wpsheeteditor.com/learndash-export-quizzes-questions-exams-google-sheets/)

## LearnDash content migration

Google Sheets can also help you prepare LearnDash data for a migration. When your content has relationships, import the parent content first and then import the content that depends on it.

1. Courses
2. Lessons
3. Topics
4. Quizzes
5. Questions

Importing the content in this order helps preserve the relationships between your LearnDash items.

## What you need

- [LearnDash LMS](https://www.liquidweb.com/software/learndash/)
- [WP Sheet Editor – Courses](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/courses-spreadsheet/)
- [Google Sheets Sync](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/google-sheets/)

pages.title: WordPress Bulk Edit Image Alt Text (Add Alt Tags in Bulk)
pages.category: Wordpress How Bulk Edit Image Seo Description
pages.content:
You can **bulk add or edit alt text or image SEO descriptions for WordPress images** by filtering your Media Library for images with missing alt tags, editing the Alt text column in a spreadsheet, applying bulk changes to multiple images, or importing alt text from a CSV file.

Table of Contents

## How to Add Alt Tags to Images in WordPress

The standard way to add alt tag or alt text to your images in WordPress is to go to the Media page in WordPress, open an image, and enter the alt text in the corresponding field.

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15133832/add-alt-tags-images-wordpress.jpg)

Unfortunately, that’s repetitive, tedious, and doesn’t let you make quick progress on your work.

## WP Sheet Editor: Your Bulk Alt Text WordPress Editor

[WP Sheet Editor – Media Library](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/) lets you quickly edit your alt tags in a spreadsheet. You can easily find all the images that don’t have alt text and add alt text to them without having to open the images one by one. You can also edit them in bulk and even export and import alt text.

You can download the plugin here:

[Download Media Library Spreadsheet Plugin](https://wpsheeteditor.com/buy-extension/?extension_id=4933&utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description#buy) - or - [Check the features](https://wpsheeteditor.com/extensions/media-files-library-spreadsheet/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description)
It turns you WordPress Media Library into a spreadsheet-style editor where you can view your media files in rows and edit fields such as:

- Image title
- Alt text (SEO description)
- Caption
- Description
- File URL
- Metadata and custom fields

**You can use the plugin as a bulk alt text editor for WordPress and WooCommerce images!** But of course, it serves many other uses!

After installing and activating the plugin, go to **Sheet Editor > Edit Media** to open the Media Library spreadsheet.

![WordPress Media Library spreadsheet for bulk editing image alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/22124556/bulk-edit-alt-text-08.png)

## Option 1: How to Change Image Alt Text in WordPress

The process for changing the alt text of your WordPress images is simple. You need to open an image that contains alt text in the WordPress Media Library and edit the text. But that’s too difficult when you want to edit many images. That’s why we’ll show you how to find images that contain specific keywords in their alt text and make bulk changes in a spreadsheet.

First, search for the images containing specific images in the alt text.

Click on **Search.**

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15153002/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-1.jpg)

Now select these values:

- **Enable advanced filters:** Yes
- **Field:** Alt Text
- **Operator:** CONTAINS
- **Value:** Enter the word you want to find. In this example, we will search for all the images containing the **T-shirt** keyword in the alternative text.
- Click on **Run search.**

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15153058/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-2.png)

The spreadsheet will display all the images matching the selected keyword.

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15153319/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-3-1.jpg)

Now you can start chaging the alt texts in the spreadsheet. Edit the alt text for all the images you want and then click on **Save.**

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15153411/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-4.jpg)

Or you can use the **Bulk Edit** tool to add a completely new alt text for all these images or replace the specific word in all images containing it.

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15154113/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-5.jpg)

### Set a new alt text for all filtered images

Select these values in the **Bulk Edit** tool:

- **Select the rows that you want to update:** Edit all the rows from my current search
- **What field do you want to edit:** Alt text
- **Select type of edit:** Set value
- **Replace existing value with this value:** Enter the new alt text here.
- Click on **Execute Now.**

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15154243/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-7.jpg)

### Replace the specific word in bulk

Select these values to replace a specific word in the alt texts:

- **Select the rows that you want to update:** Edit all the rows from my current search
- **What field do you want to edit:** Alt text
- **Select type of edit:** Replace
- **Replace this:** Enter the old word or phrase.
- **With this:** Enter the new word or phrase
- Click on **Execute Now.**

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/15154200/change-alt-text-wordpress-images-6.jpg)

## Option 2: How to Add Alt Text in Bulk to Images Missing Alt Tag

If you have many images without alt text, you can filter your Media Library to show only the images that need to be updated.

Click **Search** on the toolbar.

![WordPress Search tool for finding images missing alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28164214/open-search-images-missing-alt-tag.jpg)

Select these values to find images with missing or empty alt text:

- Tick the **Enable advanced filters** checkbox.
- **Field:** Alt text
- **Operator:** =
- **Value:** Leave this field empty.
- Click **Run search**.

![Filter WordPress Media Library images with empty alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28164153/filter-images-empty-alt-tag.png)

After you run the search, the spreadsheet will display the WordPress images that have no alt text.

![WordPress images without alt text displayed in a spreadsheet](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28164238/spreadsheet-showing-images-with-no-alt-tag.jpg)

You can also combine the alt text filter with other search filters to find a specific group of images. The **Search** tool can filter media files using fields such as:

- Keyword
- User who uploaded the file
- Keyword in title of associated post
- Post type the file is attached to
- Taxonomies in associated post
- Format
- Date
- Comment count
- Etc.

Once you have found the images you want to update, choose one of the following methods.

### Edit or Add Alt Tags Directly in the Spreadsheet

If each image needs its own alt text, you can edit the values directly in the spreadsheet.

Go to the **Alt text** column and enter the appropriate alt text for each image. This lets you give every image its own description without opening the media files individually.

When you’re finished editing the alt text, click **Save**.

![Adding alt text to WordPress images in WP Sheet Editor](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28164122/add-alt-tags-in-wp-sheet-editor.jpg)

### Use Bulk Edit to Update Multiple Images

If you want to apply the same type of change to multiple images, use the **Bulk Edit** tool. You can apply a value to all the images in your current search or to manually selected images.

![Bulk Edit tool for adding alt text to WordPress images](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28165603/open-bulk-add-alt-tags.jpg)

#### Set the Same Alt Text for Multiple Images

If several related images need the same alt text, you can set one value for all the selected images.

In the **Bulk Edit** tool, select these values:

- **Select the rows that you want to update:** Edit all the rows from my current search
- **What field do you want to edit:** Alt text
- **Select type of edit:** Set value
- **Replace existing value with this value:** Enter your new alt text here
- Click **Execute Now.**

![Set the same alt text for multiple WordPress images](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28165626/set-same-alt-tag-in-bulk.png)

After you execute the bulk edit, the selected images will have the new alt text.

#### Copy Alt Text from Another Media Library Field

You can also use **Bulk Edit** to populate the Alt text field using information that already exists in another Media Library column.

You can copy information from:

- Title
- Attached to this post
- Caption
- Filename

In the **Bulk Edit** tool, select these values:

- **Select the rows that you want to update:** Edit all the rows from my current search
- **What field do you want to edit:** Alt text
- **Select type of edit:** Copy from other columns
- **Copy from this column:** Title, Attached to this post (associated post), Caption, or Filename
- Click **Execute Now.**

![Copy information from another Media Library column to WordPress image alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28170035/copy-from-other-columns-to-alt-tag.jpg)

This is useful when the information you need is already stored in your Media Library and you want to use it to populate the Alt text field in bulk.

## Option 3: How to Import Alt Text from CSV File

If you already have alt texts prepared in a CSV file, you can import it into WP Sheet Editor to update your WordPress images.

You can also export the images you want to update, edit the alt texts or seo descriptions in Excel, Google Sheets, or another CSV editor, and then import the changes back into WordPress.

After finding the images you want to update, open the **Export** tool and download their information as a CSV file. You or your team can then add the alt text to the CSV file before importing it back into WordPress.

![wordpress-how-bulk-edit-image-seo-description](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/28193032/import-alt-text.jpg)

When you’re ready to import the file, click **Import**.

![Import WordPress image alt text from a CSV file](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28172319/import-alt-tags.jpg)

Now select the CSV file you’ll import:

- **Source:** File from my computer
- Click on **Choose File** and locate the file.
- Click on **Next.**

![Choose a CSV file containing WordPress image alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28171857/import-alt-text-2.jpg)

Now click on **Import all the columns**.

![Import all columns from a CSV file into WP Sheet Editor](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28171919/import-alt-text-3.jpg)

You need to match the rows in the CSV to the corresponding rows in your WordPress database:

- **CSV Field:** record_id
- **WordPress Field:** ID
- Click on **Next.**

![Match CSV record ID with WordPress Media Library ID during import](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28171937/import-alt-text-4.jpg)

Finally, you’ll see a preview of the changes. Check that everything is correct, then click **The preview is fine, start import.**

![Preview CSV import changes before updating WordPress image alt text](https://media.wpsheeteditor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/28171957/import-alt-text-5.png)

## How to choose a method for bulk editing WordPress image alt text

The best method depends on how you want to prepare the alt text:

- **Need Unique Alt Text for Each Image?** Edit the **Alt text** column directly in the spreadsheet.
- **Need to Apply the Same Change to Many Images?** Use the **Bulk Edit** tool.
- **Already have Useful Information in Another Media Library Field?** Use **Copy from other columns** to copy the title, associated post, caption, or filename.
- **Already have the Alt Text in a CSV File?** Import it from a CSV file.
